reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the key premises: E1 explicitly states that stable parallel phase boundaries activate atomic plane migration, promote continuous dislocation activation, provide displacement plasticity space, alleviate strain localization, and stabilize work-hardening, while E2 describes DFT simulations revealing the phase boundary-mediated toughening mechanism. premises: Stable nanoscale BCC/FCC phase boundaries enable continuous dislocation transfer
This dislocation transfer provides displacement plasticity space and mitigates strain localization
Mitigating strain localization stabilizes work-hardening and enhances toughness retention
The mechanism is distinct from nanocrystalline toughening (deflection, suppression, bridging of microcracks)
The effect is observed in nano enamel multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs)
